prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
The Green Party’s message is urgent and hopeful: in dark days of Brexit turmoil, a failing democracy and accelerating climate breakdown, the next decade is decisive. If not now, when?

Their programme is a Green New Deal to deliver both climate safety and social justice. Investing over £100 billion a year (with additional UBI funding), it puts the UK on track for net-zero by 2030 while lifting everyone up. Power and wealth are to be shared more fairly; wellbeing will replace GDP as the yardstick of progress; and no community will be left behind.

Key Green New Deal pillars:
- Energy: Replace fossil fuels with renewables; community energy; end subsidies to oil and gas; a rising Carbon Tax to render fossil fuels unviable; no fracking, no new nuclear; expand grids, storage and interconnectors.
- Housing: Insulate every home; deep retrofit 1 million buildings a year; roll out home renewables; replace gas heating; 100,000 new Passivhaus-standard council homes annually; higher standards for all new builds; protect renters and end fuel poverty.
- Transport: Make public transport cheaper than driving; electrify rail; reopen lines and expand freight by rail; empower councils to run buses and trams; build safe cycleways/footpaths; Frequent Flyer Levy; stop new runways and road-building; end sales of new petrol/diesel vehicles by 2030 with widespread EV charging.
- Industry: A circular economy with right-to-repair, ten-year warranties and bans on single-use plastics; grants and standards to decarbonise heavy industry; skills and apprenticeships; regional mutual banks; CCS for steel/cement.
- Food, farming & forestry: A ten‑year transition to agroecology; rewilding and urban greening; 700 million trees; cut pesticides; a right to food; support “less but better” meat and a fair farmer-led transition.

To make it happen, Greens will:
- Remain and reform the EU via a People’s Vote, using Europe to drive climate action, social rights, fair taxation and humane refugee policy while safeguarding freedom of movement.
- Grow democracy: proportional representation; votes at 16; an elected second chamber; citizens’ assemblies and a People’s Constitution; curb oligarchic media power; a Digital Bill of Rights; devolve power and resources to councils; a Carbon Chancellor and a Future Generations Act.

Quality of Life Guarantee: reverse austerity; invest in the NHS (+£6bn/yr) and end privatisation; expand mental and reproductive health; boost schools (+£4bn/yr); scrap tuition fees; smaller classes; restore arts and climate/nature education. Deliver secure incomes and homes with a Universal Basic Income (no one worse off), a £12 Living Wage, 35 hours free childcare from 9 months, gig worker rights, rent controls and an end to no‑fault evictions.

Justice and rights: dismantle the hostile environment; humane migration and Windrush justice; tackle discrimination and misogyny; LGBTIQA+ and disability rights; halve the prison population through prevention and restorative justice; end the war on drugs with legal, regulated supply and health-led support.

Nature and animals: a Clean Air Act; ecocide law; right to roam; more protected land and seas; end factory farming, live exports and hunting; recognise animal sentience.

Global justice: aid to 1% of GNI, climate finance and technology transfer; fair trade rules; end arms sales; a peace-first foreign policy.

Paying for it: simplify and toughen taxes on wealth and corporate profits; introduce a Land Value Tax; a rising Carbon Tax; crack down on avoidance; cancel wasteful projects (Trident, HS2, airport expansion, new roads); and borrow for productive green investment while catalysing private capital.

The Greens say they’ve been on the right side of history—and will get the future right. Every Green vote is a vote to make the Green New Deal real.
